summary.short: Zoning ordinance excerpts for Coweta County, Georgia: defines data centers and permits them as conditional uses in the LM light industrial district and as permitted uses in the M industrial district, subject to siting, buffer, noise, lighting, generator, water, sewer, power and emergency-response requirements. Effective date not stated.
summary.long: Zoning ordinance excerpts (Article 3 definitions; Article 18 LM Light Industrial and Article 19 M Industrial districts) for Coweta County, Georgia. Defines data center (up to 500,000 sq ft GFA), excludes cryptocurrency data centers, and defines data center campus and cryptocurrency mining. In the LM district, data centers are a conditional use requiring a conditional use permit from the board of commissioners after a board of zoning appeals recommendation; in the M district they are a permitted use. Both are subject to the same requirements: minimum 25-acre lot, height and setback limits, public water and sewer, a community meeting with mailed, newspaper and sign notice, building design standards, a 300-foot buffer from residential property, fencing, a pre-construction noise survey, daytime and nighttime noise limits, an environmental impact assessment, full-cutoff lighting, backup generator testing limits, a construction traffic plan, an annual waste report, equipment screening, a ban on open-loop cooling, a ban on primary onsite power generation, Tier 4 Final generator standards, substation setbacks, and emergency-response training with cost reimbursement. Violations are addressed by the county authority through written notice and other compliance action, including legal remedies; no penalty amounts are stated. The effective date is not stated in the excerpt.

notes: Document is an extract (pages 1-12, gaps marked [..]); Article 25, Article 28 and Chapter 30 are cited but not included. No adoption, effective or amendment date appears in the text, so no events are coded; the registry metadata (status, reference to 2025 moratoria) is not confirmed by the text. Data centers are conditional uses in Article 18 (Sec. 182(4)) and permitted uses in Article 19 (Sec. 191(12)) with largely parallel standards; the Article 19 community meeting applies only to properties requiring rezoning, while Article 18 does not so limit it. Numbering is irregular in the extract (two 'iv.' items in the Article 18 community meeting; Article 19 buffer items numbered iii and iv), so provision IDs follow the page layout. The 'data center' definition (Sec. 31) refers to buildings containing up to 500,000 square feet GFA and excludes cryptocurrency data centers. The 'appropriate county authority' is not named. Empty target_instrument_id and identifier fields are left blank because no registry instrument or verified identifier is named.
